properties.decision:
Anthony's ruling, 2026-09-28, in the dev_reflow2 hub, on the fixes proposed by fact:root-cause-a-sibling-designs-precedent-was-surfaced-three-times-and-never-read-2026-09-28 (he said "go with your recommendations", then chose from three options when the first recommendation turned out not to reach the failure).

THE FACT THAT CHANGED THE RECOMMENDATION. The write that missed its precedent went straight from the agent to flo2.io (flo2's design), and a registry-served engine does not reach out to another server on a caller's behalf (ReflowService::without_reaching_out; upstream_status reports such targets `refused`). reflow2's own design is still a local store beside its repository, which flo2.io cannot read at all. So req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design, built as a check inside the server being written to, could not have fired on that write. The only process that can read BOTH designs today is the hub's own local reflow2 server: it has reflow2's committed export on disk and this machine's key for api.flo2.io.

OPTIONS PUT TO HIM:
(1) SEARCH AT THE HUB — a served search that runs one query across the hub and every design it tracks and names each it could not reach; the hub skill calls it and reads what it finds before writing into any design; plus a standing rule that a claim that the design holds nothing says where it was checked. The write-time warning waits until the designs share a server.
(2) THE WRITE-TIME WARNING ANYWAY — a local design that declares its relatives checks them on every write; useful when both are on one machine, never for writes into flo2.io.
(3) SKILL AND RULE ONLY — no new tool; rests on the agent remembering, which he objected to on 2026-09-22.

CHOSE (1), "Search at the hub (Recommended)".

WHAT WAITS, AND FOR WHAT: req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design stays accepted and unbuilt until related designs are served by one host that knows their membership (for reflow2 and flo2: combined position 11, reflow2's design moving to a server). A hosted registry could then check a write against sibling designs it holds itself, without reaching out.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-09-28 — until related designs share a server, the cross-design check runs at the hub: one search across the hub and every design it tracks, read before any write; the write-time warning waits
properties.rationale: The fix has to reach the failure it is for. A check placed where it cannot see the sibling design would ship green and change nothing about the measured miss, which is the "a guard that returns a plausible list reads as a window" trap recorded in fact:the-brainstorms-only-search-was-the-write-guard-and-it-returned-only-nodes-the-session-had-just-written. Placing it at the hub puts it in the one process that can read both designs, and makes it one served call instead of a discipline repeated per design.
